author: Lars Jacobsen
html:
There will probably be some transfer of heat from one to the other - and if the cooling is inadequate the fan will run at all times. This was especially true of older notebooks running Pentium 4 cpu's that was not made for notebooks.

However most moderns cpu's wont show any erratic behaviour but will instead lower their speeds (and thereby their generation of heat) - or simply shut of to protect themself.

To make a long story short: The graphics card i probably broken :-)\
(or the driver has problems, thats often the case with notebooks)

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
html:
@Lars: Good to know that the graphics chip can handle the hot temperatures. I heard the limit for this particular FireGL v5250 is around 120 degrees Celcius.

That would worry me a bit though: there is very little distance between the CPU and the GPU

Take a look at the technical hardware maintenance manual. Page 83 shows that they almost touch corners.

Lenovo technical [hardware maintenance manual](http://www-307.ibm.com/pc/support/site.wss/document.do?lndocid=MIGR-66958) ([local copy of PDF](/wp-content/uploads/2007/11/lenovo-t60p-hardware-maintenance-manual-42t8137_01.pdf "lenovo-t60p-hardware-maintenance-manual-42t8137_01.pdf"), 3.89MB)

author: Lars Jacobsen
html: While the cooling solution seems to be lacking in quality and your card seems to be acting strangely, I should point out that most GPUs are made to run at high temperatures. Most CPUs have a threshold where they stop functioning to protect them selves, but most GPSs that I have seen runs fine at 60+

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
html: I forgot to mention: Graphics card for the T60p is ATI Mobility FireGL v5250 for the full model name

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
html: UPDATE: A technician has just replaced the graphics controller (and the entire motherboard). Since then, I have not had a single problem with external screens

author: Silencer
html: Yep, it looks like a major flaw. A guy on the forum investigated it and made a rather easy mod of the heatsink to cool GPU better: http://forum.thinkpads.com/viewtopic.php?p=372176

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
html: @Silencer After the replacement, the GPU is still running hot, but now without any problems. The GPU temp is still around 70 degrees (normally cooled) but behaves perfectly. What is really interesting (as I note in the article) is that it looks like a design flaw, that the GPU heatsink is too small to pull the heat out of the GPU and out to the fan.
